canonical_statement: The review summarizes drug treatment of acute cluster attacks, bridging therapy, and preventive treatment, while explicitly excluding neurostimulation methods.
The review states that approximately 90% of cluster headache is episodic and 10% is chronic.

population.label: People with cluster headache

canonical_statement: For acute cluster attacks, the review identifies 100% oxygen, subcutaneous sumatriptan, and intranasal sumatriptan or zolmitriptan as the principal drug treatments.

The review reports that, in a randomized placebo-controlled trial of 39 patients, 6 mg subcutaneous sumatriptan produced pain freedom or almost complete relief at 15 minutes in 74% versus 26% with placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited randomized cluster-headache trial

concept.text: Pain freedom or almost complete headache relief

canonical_statement: The same trial summary reports pain freedom at 10 minutes in 36% with 6 mg subcutaneous sumatriptan versus 3% with placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited randomized cluster-headache trial

canonical_statement: The review reports a Cochrane pooled number needed to treat of 3.3 (95% CI 2.4–5.0) for pain freedom at 15 minutes with subcutaneous sumatriptan, with pain-free rates of 48% versus 17% for placebo.

population.label: Participants pooled in the cited Cochrane analysis

canonical_statement: In a cited randomized trial of 118 patients treating 154 attacks, the review reports a 30-minute headache response of 57% with intranasal sumatriptan 20 mg versus 26% with placebo (p=0.002).

population.label: Patients in cited intranasal sumatriptan trial

outcome.definition: Decrease from very severe/severe/moderate pain to mild or none

canonical_statement: The same trial summary reports pain freedom at 30 minutes in 47% with intranasal sumatriptan 20 mg versus 18% with placebo (p=0.003).

population.label: Patients in cited intranasal sumatriptan trial

canonical_statement: The review reports bitter taste in 21% of patients after intranasal sumatriptan versus 1% after placebo in the cited trial.
The review reports that one randomized intranasal zolmitriptan trial in 92 patients produced 30-minute pain relief in 62% with 10 mg, 40% with 5 mg, and 21% with placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited zolmitriptan trial

canonical_statement: A second cited zolmitriptan trial in 52 patients is summarized as achieving 30-minute headache relief in 63% with 10 mg, 50% with 5 mg, and 30% with placebo.

population.label: Patients in second cited zolmitriptan trial

canonical_statement: The review reports a meta-analysis of 121 patients in which 30-minute headache relief occurred in 63% with zolmitriptan 10 mg, 48% with 5 mg, and 30% with placebo.

population.label: Participants in cited zolmitriptan meta-analysis

canonical_statement: The review concludes that intranasal zolmitriptan is effective for cluster attacks but is less effective in indirect comparisons than subcutaneous sumatriptan.
The review recommends 100% oxygen at at least 12 L/min, sometimes up to 15 L/min, for about 20 minutes using a non-rebreather mask; nasal cannulae are described as generally insufficient.

exposures.details: 100% oxygen via non-rebreather mask; some cases may require up to 15 L/min

canonical_statement: The review reports that a 2015 Cochrane synthesis of normobaric oxygen trials found a 75% responder rate after 15 minutes.

population.label: Participants in three cited normobaric oxygen trials

canonical_statement: The review identifies corticosteroids or greater occipital nerve corticosteroid injection as transitional therapy to bridge the period until long-term preventive treatment becomes effective, and cautions against long-term corticosteroid use because of adverse effects.
In the largest cited prednisone trial, 109 patients were analyzed and mean first-week attack counts were 7.1 with prednisone versus 9.5 with placebo while verapamil was titrated in both groups.

population.label: Analyzed patients in cited multicenter episodic cluster-headache trial

concept.text: Mean number of cluster attacks in first week

canonical_statement: The same prednisone trial summary reports adverse events in 71% of patients in both prednisone and placebo groups.
The review reports that 11 of 13 patients (85%) receiving suboccipital corticosteroid injection became attack-free in the first week, compared with 0 of 10 receiving saline placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited greater occipital nerve injection trial

canonical_statement: In a cited trial of 43 patients, 20 of 21 receiving cortivazol versus 12 of 22 receiving placebo had a mean of two or fewer daily attacks after treatment, corresponding to an odds ratio of 14.5 (95% CI 1.8–116.9; p=0.012).

population.label: Patients with more than two daily cluster attacks in cited trial

concept.text: Mean of two or fewer daily cluster attacks after injections

canonical_statement: For preventive therapy, the review states that verapamil has the strongest scientific evidence and is followed by lithium.

The review reports that a randomized placebo-controlled trial of 30 patients found verapamil 120 mg three times daily for 2 weeks significantly reduced cluster attack frequency and need for abortive treatment versus placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited episodic cluster-headache verapamil trial

concept.text: Cluster attack frequency and need for abortive treatment

canonical_statement: In a cited open verapamil series, the review reports complete relief in 49 of 52 patients with episodic cluster headache (94%).

population.label: Episodic cluster headache subgroup in cited open verapamil series

canonical_statement: In the same cited open verapamil series, the review reports complete relief in 10 of 18 patients with chronic cluster headache (55%).

population.label: Chronic cluster headache subgroup in cited open verapamil series

canonical_statement: The review reports a pair-wise meta-analysis of open-label verapamil studies in which 87% of patients achieved complete response or more than 50% reduction in attack frequency.

population.label: Participants in cited open-label verapamil meta-analysis

concept.text: Complete response or >50% reduction in attack frequency

canonical_statement: The review describes clinical verapamil initiation at 40–80 mg three times daily, with some patients requiring up to 960 mg, and recommends baseline ECG plus repeat ECG after 160-mg dose increments because of heart-block risk.

exposures.details: start 40–80 mg three times daily; some patients require up to 960 mg; ECG monitoring recommended

canonical_statement: The review reports that a meta-analysis of three open lithium trials with 103 patients found 77% achieved complete response or more than a 50% reduction in attack frequency.

population.label: Participants in cited lithium open-trial meta-analysis

concept.text: Complete response or >50% reduction in attack frequency

canonical_statement: The review notes that a placebo-controlled lithium study in episodic cluster headache was negative, while suggesting the 1-week observation period and low lithium concentrations may have contributed.

population.label: Patients in cited episodic cluster-headache lithium trial

canonical_statement: The review recommends monitoring lithium plasma concentrations plus kidney and thyroid function and gives a target lithium concentration range of 0.4–0.8 mEq/L.

exposures.details: monitor plasma concentration, kidney function, and thyroid function; target 0.4–0.8 mEq/L

canonical_statement: The review reports that, in a prospective topiramate study of 26 patients, 15 entered remission of the cluster period.

population.label: Patients in cited prospective topiramate study

canonical_statement: The same topiramate study summary reports a greater than 50% reduction in attacks in 6 of 26 patients.

population.label: Patients in cited prospective topiramate study

concept.text: Greater than 50% reduction in cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The review considers topiramate a possible alternative when verapamil or lithium is ineffective or not tolerated, but emphasizes that supporting data are from open observational studies.

The review reports that a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled sodium valproate study of 96 patients found no statistically significant difference from placebo for the primary endpoint of at least a 50% reduction in weekly cluster attacks.

population.label: Patients in cited sodium valproate trial

concept.text: At least 50% reduction in mean weekly cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The review concludes that there is no scientific evidence establishing sodium valproate as effective for cluster headache.
The review reports that a small study of 14 patients treated with gabapentin for 3.5 months produced a mean 45% reduction in cluster attacks.

population.label: Patients in cited gabapentin study

canonical_statement: The review states that evidence for gabapentin is limited to small open-label observational series, with possible benefit in some patients with refractory chronic cluster headache.
The review reports that a double-blind placebo-controlled melatonin trial of 20 patients found 5 of 10 patients receiving melatonin 10 mg nightly were responders.

population.label: Patients in cited melatonin trial

concept.text: Responder status based on reduction in cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The review reports that, in an episodic cluster headache trial of 106 patients, attack frequency during the first 3 weeks decreased by 52% with galcanezumab versus 27% with placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited episodic cluster-headache galcanezumab trial

canonical_statement: The review reports that a chronic cluster headache trial of 237 patients found a mean weekly attack reduction of 5.4 with galcanezumab versus 4.6 with placebo, a difference that was not statistically significant.

population.label: Patients in cited chronic cluster-headache galcanezumab trial

concept.text: Mean weekly reduction in cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The review concludes that galcanezumab efficacy had been demonstrated for episodic but not chronic cluster headache.

The review reports that, in an open ketamine-magnesium series of 17 refractory chronic cluster headache patients, daily attacks fell from 4.3±2.4 to 1.3±1.0, a mean difference of −3.1 attacks/day (95% CI −4.5 to −1.6; p<0.001).

population.label: Refractory chronic cluster headache patients in cited ketamine-magnesium series

concept.text: Change in number of daily cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The same ketamine-magnesium series summary reports 13 responders among 17 treated patients.

population.label: Refractory chronic cluster headache patients in cited ketamine-magnesium series

canonical_statement: The review reports mild sedation in 41.2% of patients in the cited ketamine-magnesium series.
The review characterizes ketamine as a possible future option that requires placebo-controlled validation and notes its addiction potential.
The review reports that a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase II pasireotide trial was discontinued after 28 patients because of lack of efficacy.

population.label: Patients in cited pasireotide phase II trial

canonical_statement: The review reports that an open onabotulinumtoxinA trial in 17 men with chronic cluster headache found a greater than 50% reduction in cumulative headache minutes in 59% of participants.

population.label: Male chronic cluster headache patients in cited onabotulinumtoxinA trial

concept.text: Greater than 50% reduction in cumulative headache minutes

canonical_statement: A second open-label onabotulinumtoxinA study in 10 subjects is summarized as finding no statistically significant reduction in weekly attacks at month 2 compared with baseline.

population.label: Subjects in cited otic-ganglion onabotulinumtoxinA pilot study

canonical_statement: The review describes a 496-participant Clusterbusters medication-use survey in which indoleamine hallucinogens were reported as comparable to or more efficacious than most conventional medications, while recognizing this as survey evidence rather than controlled-trial evidence.

population.label: Respondents to cited Clusterbusters medication-use survey

concept.text: Self-reported shortening or abortion of a cluster period

canonical_statement: The review reports that, in a Danish real-life cohort, 20% of 30 patients using subcutaneous sumatriptan reported a 100% treatment effect and a further 10% reported 50% pain relief.

population.label: Patients in cited Danish cohort using subcutaneous sumatriptan

concept.text: Self-reported treatment effect for cluster attacks

canonical_statement: The review reports that only 20% of patients in the cited Danish cohort reported being responders to verapamil prophylaxis.

population.label: Patients in cited Danish cohort reporting verapamil prophylaxis response

canonical_statement: The review emphasizes that preventive cluster-headache evidence contains very few placebo-controlled studies and that most data for therapies other than verapamil and lithium come from open studies.
The review identifies spontaneous ending of episodic cluster bouts and a relatively high placebo response as major challenges for preventive-treatment trial design and interpretation.
The review concludes that additional effective, well-tolerated fast-acting therapies and preventive therapies are needed for cluster headache.
Open-access funding for the review was enabled and organized by Projekt DEAL.

Hans Christoph Diener reported honoraria from Ipsen, Lilly, Lundbeck, Novartis, Pfizer, and Teva for clinical-trial participation, advisory-board contributions, or oral presentations, and reported institutional/research roles and support as listed in the declaration.
Arne May reported being editor of Cephalalgia and reported no conflicts of interest.
The review states that availability of data and material is not applicable.
